A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPARC and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained material can be matched across appendix renumbering and table consolidation.

before.justification: V1 reports original captioning experiments, human evaluations, attention analyses and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds grounding measurements, efficiency experiments, further sensitivity analyses and POPE evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same EMA-based relative activation score, token selection, cumulative selection counts and cached-value amplification, with unchanged Equations 1–9. The caption-first POPE setup extends evaluation without revising SPARC's attention-calibration procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds a supplementary POPE evaluation involving caption-conditioned object-presence questions and instruction following. The original detailed-captioning coverage on IIW-400, DOCCI and MS-COCO remains unchanged.

E2.justification: OPERA, VCD, VOLCANO and PAI remain the comparators in the retained caption-quality experiments. New efficiency and POPE comparisons reuse existing methods, including the previously evaluated naive attention-scaling approach; no comparator is added or removed within a retained experiment.

E3.justification: V2 substantially extends evaluation design with object-mask attention scoring on 5,000 COCO images, gradient-weighted and token-normalized diagnostics, latency measurement, and four-parameter sweeps on 500 DOCCI images for two additional models. POPE introduces caption-first prompting, accuracy restricted to instruction-compliant responses, and an instruction-following metric. Original captioning protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component ablations, attention-sink and caption-diversity analyses, v2 adds semantic-region grounding measurements, saliency checks and token-count normalization (Table 5; Figures 12–13). Appendix C extends four-parameter CLAIR sensitivity studies to LLaVA-NeXT and Qwen2-VL, while Appendix E examines instruction following. These substantially broaden validation of the method's mechanism and sensitivity.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports timing measurements with ± terms in Table 6, although their statistical meaning and repetition count are unspecified. Both versions already report five repetitions for CHAIR and Q1–Q3 bands in Figure 5; no increase in those run counts is stated.

E6.justification: Headline Tables 1–4 and the original CHAIR results remain unchanged. Substantial additions include relevant-region attention of 17.85%, 15.50% and 19.17% for baseline, naive scaling and SPARC; baseline/SPARC latency of 30.37/31.21 ms per token; further parameter-sweep results; and conditional POPE accuracies of 82.01%, 81.45% and 83.13%. New diagnostic figures also report saliency and normalized-attention findings.

T1.justification: The method equations, caption-similarity definition and CHAIR formulas are retained. V2's additional attention diagnostics introduce empirical measurements, without adding or revising formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or theoretical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: existing hallucination mitigation sacrifices recall, while training-free SPARC improves precision and recall with minimal overhead. New experiments support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies background tokens as potentially carrying global context and discusses limitations of interpreting raw attention and unnormalized attention totals. It also adds interpretations concerning tuning and POPE instruction following. The existing limitation concerning early-caption hallucinations and CHAIRs is retained in Appendix F.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code repository link, RTX8000 hardware information, latency-measurement details and a float16 attention-state memory estimate below 40 KB. It also documents segmentation masks, gradient weighting, additional parameter ranges and the POPE comparator's scaling setting. Existing SPARC implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting attention interpretation, segmentation-based analysis and caption-based reasoning, including Darcet, Zhang, Ren, Ravi and Mitra. The anonymous visual-attention-sink citation becomes Kang et al., referring to the same work. The central positioning against hallucination mitigation and naive attention amplification remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites Sections 3.2–3.3, organizes Section 5.3 with descriptive subheadings, and adds acknowledgements, an impact statement and a POPE appendix. Author information and some wording are corrected. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: The display set substantially expands with grounding and timing tables, cross-model sensitivity tables, POPE tables, and saliency and normalized-attention figures. V1 Tables 6–9 are consolidated into v2 Table 8 without changing their values. Existing plots are retained and renumbered where needed, alongside conference-style title formatting and running headers.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central mechanism and efficiency claims. Semantic-region measurements, saliency checks and token-count normalization address weaknesses in v1's reliance on raw and aggregate attention, while Table 6 supplies previously missing runtime evidence. Broader sensitivity studies further support assessment across models. POPE accuracy remains limited by compliance-based filtering, and timing uncertainty is insufficiently explained, but these limitations do not outweigh the stronger validation of the paper's central arguments.
